11 minutes|yungblud \u0026 halsey (feat..note: Released by Locomotion Recordings and Geffen Records on February 13, 2019, '11 Minutes' is a collaboration by English musician Yungblud and American singer-songwriter Halsey, featuring American musician Travis Barker of Blink-182. The listener enjoys this track as a modern take on alt-rock and pop-punk with great hooks and heavy drums, appreciating the collaborations between Halsey and Travis Barker alongside the rap-like elements.

barrel of a gun|guster.note: Featured on the 1999 album Lost and Gone Forever, where all the drums were played by hand without sticks, this track captures the listener's memory of seeing the Boston band open for Barenaked Ladies in the mid-'90s with their signature hand percussion and '4, 3, 2, 1' hook. The listener places this song around 1999 in their own life.

basket case|green day.note: "Basket Case" is a song by the American rock band Green Day, released on August 1, 1994, by Reprise Records as the second single from the band's third studio album, Dookie. This listener associates the track with the early fall of dating a now-wife at the Boston Hatch Shell, where a free concert overwhelmed security and was cut short after barely playing one song.

brick|ben folds five.note: Released by alternative rock group Ben Folds Five as a single from their album Whatever and Ever Amen, Brick became one of the band's biggest hits with mainstream radio play in the US, the UK, and Australia. This listener connected the piano-based rock track to an unexpected geographical tie-in, feeling that the song served as a sign about relocating to North Carolina.

colors|halsey.note: Released as a single from her debut studio album Badlands, Colors showcases the modern synth-pop style that initially drew this listener to Halsey's music. The listener appreciates how the catchy, synth-heavy track echoes the 1980s alternative sounds of their youth as part of their enduring fandom across the artist's diverse musical eras.

crazy for you|madonna.note: Originally released in 1985 from the soundtrack to the film Vision Quest and later included on the compilation album Celebration, this pop ballad marked a departure from Madonna's earlier dance-oriented material and became her second number-one single on the US Billboard Hot 100. This listener remembers it as one of the first early love ballads they loved, standing out in the collection mostly because of Madonna's singing voice.

deep cover|dr. dre and snoop dogg.note: Released in 1992 as the lead single from the soundtrack to the film of the same name, this hardcore track marked the explosive solo debut of Snoop Dogg over a hypnotic Dr. Dre beat. For this listener, who started college while remaining attached to their hometown and following a different path than their childhood pals, the song preserves the thrill of Snoop's arrival alongside the enduring legacy of N.W.A from their high school years.

demons|imagine dragons.note: Released as a single from the debut studio album Night Visions, "Demons" by Imagine Dragons became a major commercial success and spent twelve weeks in the top ten on the Billboard Hot 100. This listener associates the ubiquitous 2010s melodic rock anthem with radio play, games, and family car rides with the kids.

desperately wanting|better than ezra.note: Desperately Wanting is a song by American alternative rock group Better Than Ezra that was released in November 1996 as the second single from their third studio album, Friction, Baby, and became a chart hit in the United States, Australia, and Canada. This listener associates the track with a memorable live performance at Lupo's in Providence during the mid-1990s, where an amazing balcony view enhanced the experience of seeing the band with a spouse.

dreams|van halen.note: Released in 1986 as the second single from Van Halen's album 5150, "Dreams" reached number 22 on the US Billboard Hot 100, driven by its prominent synthesizer hooks and Sammy Hagar's soaring vocals. This listener fondly recalls discovering the track likely on MTV during middle school, appreciating how the band blended hard rock with a novel keyboard-heavy sound.

enjoy the silence|depeche mode.note: Released as the second single from the album Violator, this track became Depeche Mode's best-selling single and won Best British Single at the Brit Awards 1991. The listener associates the song with the end of high school, remembering its great guitar riff over electronic beats and the classic MTV video featuring a king with a deck chair.

eye of the tiger|survivor.note: Written by Frankie Sullivan and Jim Peterik as the theme song for the 1982 film Rocky III and released that May as a single from Survivor's third album, Eye of the Tiger, the track combines hard rock with a post-disco beat and reached number one on the charts of many countries. This listener associates the arena rock track with early musical memories tied to movies, specifically recalling boxing scenes and a later film featuring Ivan Drago.

footloose|kenny loggins.note: Released in January 1984 as the first of two singles by Kenny Loggins from the film of the same name, "Footloose" spent three weeks at number one on the US Billboard Hot 100. This listener associates the track with childhood memories on prospect street, capturing a small town feel and the joy of the movie's dance ending.

heartspark dollarsign|everclear.note: Originally appearing on Everclear's 1995 major-label debut album Sparkle and Fade, "Heartspark Dollarsign" serves as a nostalgic anchor for the listener, recalling a bittersweet Boston Xmas rave concert that marked one of the final shows shared with a college roommate.

here comes a regular|the replacements.note: Here Comes a Regular appears on the 1985 album Tim, which was produced by Tommy Erdelyi and marked the final album featuring the original line-up of the band. The listener connects this track to a vacation in Wilmington with Mike and Jess, associating the city both with filming locations for One Tree Hill and subsequent set tours.

hey ya|outkast.note: Released by Outkast in 2003 as part of the double album Speakerboxxx/The Love Below, "Hey Ya!" became a massive global chart-topper and defined the pop landscape of the era. The listener associates this upbeat track and its iconic music video with holding their first newborn son and working out while he slept.

home sweet home|mötley crüe.note: Released in 1985 on Mötley Crüe's album Theatre of Pain, 'Home Sweet Home' became a defining anthem of the 1980s heavy metal power ballad era. For the listener, the track captures the bittersweet transition of starting middle school and gaining independence, perfectly mirroring the feeling of moving on.

i think we're alone now|tiffany.note: Tiffany released her cover of I Think We're Alone Now as the second single from her debut studio album, Tiffany, and the track spent two weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart. The listener associates this song with their freshman year of high school and their first concert attended with cousins and a sister, recalling when Tiffany and Debbie Gibson arrived as popular mall performers of that era.

i'll be|edwin mccain.note: Edwin McCain released the song on his album Misguided Roses, and it eventually reached number five in the United States and number 52 in Canada. The listener associates the track with the bittersweet period when college roommates moved to different states around 1998, serving as a reminder of their time together and the start of new chapters in their lives.

joey|concrete blonde.note: Released in 1990 as the lead single from Concrete Blonde's album Bloodletting, "Joey" became a major alternative rock hit and spent several weeks at the top of the Billboard Modern Rock Tracks chart. For this listener, the track evokes memories of driving around southeastern Massachusetts on the way to see his then-girlfriend, a connection sparked after discovering the song through the early years of the television show 90210.

love song|the cure.note: Released in 1989 as part of The Cure's landmark album Disintegration, "Lovesong" became the band's highest-charting single on the US Billboard Hot 100. MTV introduced this track to the listener, whose college roommate later deepened their appreciation for British alternative music.

mayonaise|smashing pumpkins.note: Released in 1993 on the Smashing Pumpkins' breakthrough album Siamese Dream, "Mayonaise" remains one of the band's most celebrated alternative rock anthems. This listener connects the track to fond memories of seeing the band live at Lollapalooza with a college roommate who loved the album.

monsters (feat. blackbear)|all time low.note: Featured on the eighth studio album Wake Up, Sunshine, the song became the highest-charting single of the band's career. The listener enjoys this track as a modern 2020s crossover that blends the band's earlier emo-pop style with rap hooks from blackbear.

more than words|extreme.note: Released as an acoustic rock ballad by the American rock band Extreme from their second album, Pornograffitti, this song topped the Billboard Hot 100 chart. For this listener, it captures the combination of high school prom, the end of high school, heading to college in the fall, and the interesting detail that the band was Boston-based.

my name is jonas|weezer.note: Serving as the explosive opening track to Weezer's 1994 self-titled debut, 'My Name Is Jonas' transitions seamlessly from gentle acoustic picking into a heavy, melodic rock anthem. This listener fondly recalls how those dynamic guitar shifts provided a fitting soundtrack just as their college years were coming to a close.

nightswimming|r.e.m..note: Released in 1993 on the album Automatic for the People, R.E.M.'s "Nightswimming" features a poignant piano arrangement by bassist Mike Mills complemented by Michael Stipe's evocative vocals. For this listener, who first fell in love with alternative music through the band, the track served as close college friends' wedding song and continues to evoke deep memories of that joyful day alongside reflections on love and friendship.

papercut|linkin park.note: Released as the third single from Linkin Park's diamond-certified 2000 debut album Hybrid Theory, "Papercut" peaked at number 14 on the UK Singles Chart. For this listener, who transitioned from an urban rap background to grunge-loving private university peers during a period of major life changes, the track's unique blend of hip-hop and alternative rock perfectly bridged two different worlds.

regret|new order.note: Released in 1993 as the lead single from New Order's album Republic, "Regret" became a major alternative radio hit and reached number 28 on the US Billboard Hot 100. This listener associates the track with being introduced to '80s British alternative music by a college roommate around 1993, blending those sounds with '90s rock and grunge.

rock of ages|def leppard.note: Rock of Ages is a song by Def Leppard from their 1983 album Pyromania. This listener connects the track to fond memories of their friend Peter and the historical resilience of the band's drummer.

running from my shadow|mike shinoda (fea.note: This track appears on the 2018 debut solo album Post Traumatic, which consists of songs about Mike Shinoda's feelings following the death of Chester Bennington, his Linkin Park bandmate. The listener fondly recalls hearing this album shortly after Chester's death as a meaningful expression of pain, cherishing the memory of seeing the artist play live in Raleigh with a spouse.

scenario|a tribe called quest.note: Released in 1992 on A Tribe Called Quest's album The Low End Theory, "Scenario" featured an iconic breakout guest verse by Busta Rhymes over hard-hitting production. This track soundtracked the listener's dorm life and college years, remaining in heavy rotation alongside grunge despite changing musical trends.

silent running|mike + the mechanics.note: Released in late 1985 as the lead single from Mike + The Mechanics' self-titled debut album, "Silent Running" reached number six on the US Billboard Hot 100 in 1986. For this listener, the track serves as a musical anchor to Prospect Street and childhood sports memories, evoking a timeless bond with a lifelong friend from that neighborhood.

smells like teen spirit|nirvana.note: "Smells Like Teen Spirit" is the opening track and lead single from Nirvana's second album, Nevermind (1991), released on DGC Records, and it propelled the album to the top of several charts while helping grunge enter the mainstream. The listener associates this track with dorm life and freshman year, reflecting on growing up, childhood friends moving on, the weight of life-trajectory choices, and balancing home and college life while feeling broke.

someday i suppose|mighty mighty bosstone.note: Released in 1993 on the album "Don't Know How to Party," the Mighty Mighty Bosstones' track "Someday I Suppose" exemplifies the high-energy ska-punk fusion that defined the Boston band's signature sound. For this listener, the song evokes a vivid memory of a sweaty, intense New Year's Eve concert at the Middle East basement, perfectly matching the track's driving rhythm and catchy aggression.

something's always wrong|toad the wet sp.note: Released in 1994 on Toad the Wet Sprocket's album Dulcinea, "Something's Always Wrong" reached number four on the US Modern Rock Tracks chart. For this listener, the track serves as a lasting anchor to college friendships formed around the band and unforgettable nights at the Orpheum Theater.

somewhere only we know|keane.note: Somewhere Only We Know is a song composed and performed by English alternative rock band Keane, and it appears on their debut album, Hopes and Fears. The listener connects with this melodic and memorable track as a calming song that bridges different family music tastes sparked by watching Glee.

summer|buffalo tom.note: Buffalo Tom released the track "Summer" on their 1995 album "Sleepy Eyed". For this listener, the song is permanently intertwined with a final concert before a friend moved to Arizona, following a memorable moment when Greg was pulled onto the stage.

teenage love|slick rick.note: Released in 1988 on Slick Rick's acclaimed debut album The Great Adventures of Slick Rick, this classic hip-hop track captures the vulnerable and humorous side of teenage romance. For the listener, the song served as an anthem for an awkward high school era of self-discovery and yearning for a first relationship.

the freshmen|verve pipe.note: "The Freshmen" by the American alternative rock band the Verve Pipe was released as the third single from their second studio album Villains, becoming the group's breakthrough hit and highest-charting single. For this listener, the track is permanently intertwined with a painful breakup period in 1996 when a then-girlfriend considered ending the relationship and the listener went to stay at a friend's place for the first time after college.

the old apartment|barenaked ladies.note: Featured on the albums Born on a Pirate Ship, Rock Spectacle and Disc One: All Their Greatest Hits, this track by the Canadian alternative rock group Barenaked Ladies became the band's first entry on the US Billboard Hot 100. The listener connects the song to their post-college years in Arlington and Waltham, remembering a concert attended with friends who loved the band and saw them perform alongside Guster.

there is a light that never goes out|the.note: Featured on the Smiths' 1986 album The Queen is Dead, "There Is a Light That Never Goes Out" has endured as one of the band's most celebrated tracks. This listener discovered the song through a college roommate during their junior year, instantly drawn to the intelligent lyrics and the singer's confident delivery.

thnks fr th mmrs|fall out boy.note: Released in 2007 on Fall Out Boy's album Infinity on High, 'Thnks fr th Mmrs' became a prominent mid-2000s pop-punk radio hit and a defining anthem of the era. The listener associates this high-energy, catchy track with nostalgia, pairing it with other emo staples like 'I Write Sins Not Tragedies' and connecting its era to memories of watching One Tree Hill.

tiny dancer|elton john.note: Released on Elton John's 1971 album Madman Across the Water, "Tiny Dancer" features legendary backing vocals and instrumentation that elevate its sweeping melody. The listener connects this classic track to the iconic tour bus scene in the film Almost Famous, which evokes a bittersweet memory of feeling at home in North Carolina while bonding over the movie's unforgettable characters and music.

title and registration|death cab for cut.note: Title and Registration is a song by indie rock band Death Cab for Cutie, appearing on their fourth studio album Transatlanticism. This listener connected with the track's witty opening observation about glove compartments and souvenirs, recalling their introduction to the band around 2003.

welcome to the terrordome|public enemy.note: Public Enemy recorded "Welcome to the Terrordome" for their 1990 album Fear of a Black Planet, and released it as a single in January 1990 according to discographer Martin C. Strong. This high-energy track resonates with the listener's fond memories of playing it on the way to an amusement park and being introduced to rap music by their cousin.

with or without you|u2.note: Released as the lead single from The Joshua Tree, this rock ballad features sustained guitar parts played with a prototype of the Infinite Guitar alongside Bono's vocals and Adam Clayton's bassline. While living in a heavily Irish Boston, this listener felt that U2 was adopted by the local music scene and experienced the song as extremely powerful in both its lyrics and musical arrangement.

would?|alice in chains.note: Written by Jerry Cantrell as a tribute to Andrew Wood and featured on the Singles: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack and the album Dirt, "Would?" became a definitive grunge anthem. The listener fondly recalls this track as their favorite from the Cameron Crowe movie's soundtrack, perfectly capturing the spirit of the era.

zombie|the cranberries.note: Zombie is a protest song by the Irish alternative rock band the Cranberries from their second studio album, No Need to Argue, featuring grunge-style distorted guitar and shouted vocals. This listener connects the track to the spring of 1995 in Rhode Island during college graduation week, when a surreal mosh pit broke out with the listener's brother-in-law.
